key_insight: CTLink connects written chest CT findings to their locations in a 3D scan. It uses text prompts to segment the abnormalities described in radiology reports.
problem_solved: Radiology reports describe abnormalities without marking them on the scan, leaving readers to determine which image regions correspond to each finding.
method: Use report finding text as a prompt for 3D segmentation of the corresponding abnormality.
Train on 4,123 noncontrast chest CT scans containing 9,547 segmented report findings.
Include ReXGroundingCTv2, a newly annotated dataset of 1,134 scans and 1,895 findings.
impact: CTLink offers a way to ground clinical language in volumetric medical images, potentially supporting interactive scan review and report-linked visualization. The provided abstract excerpt does not include performance results.
visual_elements: Workflow diagram: report finding → CTLink → highlighted region in a 3D chest CT.
Side-by-side report excerpt and CT slices with matching color-coded segmentation overlays.
Training-data graphic showing 4,123 scans and 9,547 segmented findings.
Dataset spotlight card for ReXGroundingCTv2: 1,134 scans and 1,895 findings.
paper_title: CTLink: A Text-Prompted Segmentation Model for Linking Radiology Report Findings to 3D Chest CT Scans
paper_authors: Mohammed Baharoon, Sung Eun Kim, Mahmoud Hussain Alabbad, Lucas Bijnens, Ali Piracha
